content:
#48 Thanks for telling me the current situation.

Thank you for the LLM advice, it is useful as I now learned there is no fairly reliable/algorithmic solution. Free versions have here a number of glitches, even when the prompt is careful and insist on not skipping stuff (e.g. retains iTeX commands not from ordinary LaTeX like \lt, does not recognize emphasis like boldface in the source (it does if one gives the URL of the show page, but then it sometimes does not as it can not always get the server response and then it uses index file with multiple errors and format omissions), the hyperref have mixed behaviour etc. The fact that the reaction to a prompt is somewhat unpredictable is a problem if one is using on a number of pages (I am not saying to complain but to inform other people who might try.) I wanted from the large number of my teaching pages in my personal lab to produce some sort of a decent integral file on a sequence of 5 elementary courses (math for elem. school teachers).

Recently I wanted to retype math and translate Pierre Gabriel's thesis from French, I think it is still a very useful reference (a number of results there were somehow not noticed by a number of people who redone the same results in less elegant ways though 1960-s which produced also much of terminological confusion and wrong historical attributions). I done 1/5 manually, and now would like the rest with OCR+LLMs (OCRs are bad with formulas unless specialized/advanced machine or program). There is a paid version which allegedly can do it from pdf or djvu scan (OCR and the LaTeXing together), with free versions there are problems in practice if one wants to anything more than a couple of pages and not to work very hard on making 1/3 of manual work.
